status_legend.active: This is the single current work item.

features.title: Inventory and analyze the complete learning corpus
features.behavior: Every file in the read-only source folder is inventoried, readable, analyzed, and traceable.
verification: Recursively count all source entries and files.
Read every file as UTF-8.
Hash every file and check exact duplicates.
Inspect links, embeds, attachments, and near-duplicate structure.
Record the result in docs/source-inventory.md and docs/source-analysis.md.
evidence: 65 unique source IDs match 65 current source paths and SHA-256 prefixes
features.notes: The source folder was not modified.

features.title: Freeze the lite profile and traceability contract
features.behavior: A maintainer can identify every core component, why it exists, when it applies, and which sources justify it.
verification: Review docs/design-proposal.md for core, optional, and deferred components.
Confirm every proposed component has source references and an adoption trigger.
Confirm trade-offs and rollback paths are explicit.
features.notes: This establishes the design baseline, not the finished adopter template.

features.title: Implement a dependency-free baseline validator
features.behavior: Running ./init.sh validates the current starter control plane without installing dependencies.
verification: Run ./init.sh from the repository root.
Confirm required artifacts exist.
Confirm feature_list.json is valid and respects WIP and evidence rules.

features.title: Build the Core profile, configuration, state transitions, and fixture
features.behavior: A new project can safely install the Core profile, configure command arrays, transition state with receipts, and pass a cold-start test.
verification: Copy the profile into an empty fixture repository.
Configure setup, start, focused verification, and full verification.
Open a fresh session and answer the five cold-start questions from repository files only.
Run the standard startup path twice to confirm idempotence.
Exercise activate, block, reopen, passing, and WIP=1 behavior.
evidence: ./init.sh -> Core profile audit healthy and 8 fixture tests passing (2026-07-25)
features.notes: Python 3.10+ is the only Core runtime dependency; project commands execute without a shell.

features.title: Add layered completion and clean-state gates
features.behavior: A feature cannot pass without the verification levels required by its risk and without a resumable clean state.
verification: Exercise static, runtime, integration, and end-to-end gate selections in fixtures.
Confirm a failing required gate prevents passing.
Confirm actionable failure messages identify what, why, and how to fix.
Confirm a regression can demote a previously passing feature.
evidence: ./init.sh -> V0-V4, failure, clean-state, state-sync, and risk-downgrade fixtures passing (2026-07-25)
features.notes: Completion runs contiguous levels from V0 through the selected profile and records skipped levels.

features.title: Harden verification, evidence freshness, installation, traceability, and release lifecycle
features.behavior: A copied Core profile executes feature-specific verification, rejects stale evidence and unsafe install paths, resolves every learning source locally, bounds command execution, and supports versioned install, upgrade, and removal.
verification: Bind every feature verification requirement to executable gates or commands and reject unbound requirements.
Reject passing receipts when receipt, configuration, verification, revision, or tracked file digests are stale or structurally incomplete.
Reject symbolic links in every existing target segment and any managed install path that resolves outside the target root.
Validate a 65-entry source disposition ledger and copy a self-contained source map with the Core profile.
Exercise timeout, cwd, bounded logs, missing executables, and representative generic, Python, and Node project fixtures.
Exercise versioned install, safe upgrade, dry-run removal, rollback, license, and notice contracts.
Run ./init.sh and confirm every dynamic fixture passes without temporary artifacts.
evidence: ./init.sh -> required artifacts 30/30, live source traceability 65/65, Core self-audit, and 27 dynamic Fixture tests passing (2026-07-25)

tests/test_core_profile.py -> executable bindings, immutable WIP/receipt rules, schema-v2 receipt digest/structure, config/verification/tracked-file freshness, and real Git ancestor/divergence checks passing (2026-07-25)
tests/test_core_profile.py -> timeout with child process-group termination, inside/outside cwd, missing executable, bounded/redacted logs, POSIX, Python, and Node fixtures passing (2026-07-25)

tests/test_core_profile.py -> target/ancestor/descendant symlink refusal, real 0.1.0->0.1.1 replacement, downgrade/pre-1 minor refusal, replacement and partial-create failure rollback, dry-run removal, manual-merge acknowledgement, backup, and modified-file refusal passing (2026-07-25)
scripts/validate_harness.py -> 65-row inventory/disposition/source-map identity, decision/target parity, reverse component links, SemVer, LICENSE, and NOTICE validation passing (2026-07-25)
features.notes: At HST-007 completion, POSIX shell and Python 3.10+ were the support boundary. HST-008 supersedes that boundary with a native Windows adapter while preserving the HST-007 evidence as historical proof.

features.title: Add a native Windows PowerShell and process-control adapter
features.behavior: A copied Core profile initializes from PowerShell, resolves a supported Python launcher, executes portable built-in gates, and terminates timed-out process trees safely on native Windows without weakening POSIX behavior.
verification: Install init.ps1 as a traced Core component and validate its launcher, PowerShell -Setup to Python --setup forwarding, working-directory, and exit-code contract.
Replace distribution-owned gate interpreter paths with a portable current-Python token while preserving shell-free argv execution.
Use Windows process-group creation and taskkill tree termination on nt while retaining POSIX session and signal behavior.
Exercise portable argv expansion, simulated Windows process options and termination fallback, path rejection, and PowerShell contract fixtures.
Document native Windows adoption, support boundaries, execution policy guidance, rollback, and the unverified-on-Windows limitation when no Windows runner is available.
Run ./init.sh and all existing POSIX, lifecycle, receipt, source, and representative-stack fixtures without regression.
evidence: ./init.sh -> required artifacts 32/32, live source traceability 65/65, Core self-audit, and 37 dynamic Fixture tests discovered: 36 passed, 1 explicit non-Windows PowerShell test skipped (2026-07-25)

tests/test_core_profile.py -> PowerShell 5.1 launcher/setup/cwd/exit-code static contract passing; native adapter test is mandatory when PowerShell is present and explicitly skipped on this macOS host (2026-07-25)

tests/test_core_profile.py -> {python} argv[0] expansion/position rejection, schema-v3 runtime freshness, internal argv/tracked digest checks, and schema-v2 historical re-verification migration passing (2026-07-25)

tests/test_core_profile.py -> simulated nt creation flags, Windows quoting, CTRL_BREAK/taskkill/direct-kill order, actual POSIX child-group timeout, and bounded runner regressions passing (2026-07-25)
tests/test_core_profile.py -> symlink and simulated junction/reparse refusal, Windows case alias/reserved name/ADS/trailing segment rejection, and lifecycle rollback regressions passing (2026-07-25)
docs/source-disposition.md + Core source-map/components -> 65 disposition rows, declared broad-vs-direct link semantics, and HC-018 exact coverage passing (2026-07-25)
features.notes: This is a Core portability adapter, not part of optional HST-006 governance and observability. The current host has no pwsh/powershell, so native PowerShell parsing/execution, real taskkill, and a real Windows junction remain unexecuted locally. These checks are retained as future verification evidence when a Windows/PowerShell runner is available; they are not pending implementation or a Core 0.2.0 completion blocker.

features.title: Package optional advanced governance and observability modules
features.behavior: Larger repositories can opt into plans, product specs, quality scoring, security, observability, and role separation without bloating the core profile.
verification: Install each optional module independently in a fixture.
Confirm core startup remains valid when the module is absent.
Run an ablation benchmark and retain only modules with measurable value.
features.notes: Intentionally out of scope for Core 0.2.0 by user decision on 2026-07-25. Reconsider only when a future release explicitly re-scopes an observed governance or observability bottleneck; this is not pending work for the current release.
